newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end firm, seen gaining next week.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end firm, seen gaining next week.

text.p: Austrian bonds ended a calm session firm on Friday, with trade revolving almost exclusively around the German Bund future due to a lack of clients, traders said and forecast upside next week.
"Clients were only interested in Germany, to see whether the Bund future would aim for 103," said one trader.

Dealers predicted the German Bund future would trade in a narrow range between 102.50 and 103,50. Since profit-taking had been relatively restrained ahead of the weekend the chances of further gains were seen as good, they said.
* 10-year benchmark 5.625 pct bond maturing July 2007 up 15 bps at 100.30 to yield 5.58 (5.60) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.31/41 to yield 5.58/5.57 pct.
* Five-year 4.625 bond maturing May 2002 steady at 100.30 to yield 4.55 pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.28/36 to yield 4.56/54 percent.
* Austrian bond future up three bps at 110.15 on turnover of 240 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany up one at six bps, five-year spread down one at 18 bps.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.393 and overnight money at 3.13/3.38. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
